learning_outcomes.text: Understand an organization, the different functional areas of management and how they are interconnected.
Be aware of main management concepts, methods and tools.
Be able to analyze and apply management methods and tools in real contexts.
Understand the importance of behavioral competencies in the organizational and work context.
Be able to solve some production operations management problems through appropriated tools and techniques application

syllabus_topics: BASIC CONCEPTS: THE COMPANY AND THE MANAGEMENT
Companies, Management and the role of the Manager
The management process: Planning, Organization, Leadership and Control
Management levels: Strategic management and functional policies.
Elements of organizational design: chain and unit of command, span of control, centralisation and decentralisation, vertical and horizontal coordination, etc
Basic structures: functional, geographical, divisional, mixed, matrix.
FUNCTIONAL AREAS OF MANAGEMENT: FUNDAMENTAL CONCEPTS
Marketing Management: market; fundamental marketing concepts; the marketing mix.
People Management: the human resources function; motivation; leadership.
Operations management: Fundamentals of operations management; production processes; types of layouts; Quality Management.
Financial management: Introduction to financial management; basic accounting principles; break-even point.
DECISION SUPPORT IN INDUSTRIAL OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT
Forecasting: regression; simple and moving averages; exponential smoothing.
Inventory Control: economic order quantity; deterministic replenishment models.
Production Planning: production to order; lot production; MRP method; JIT systems
teaching_methods: Theoretical lectures focusing on fundamental management concepts and tools.
Practical classes focusing on real case study analysis and discussion, emphasizing the application of management concepts and tools.
Group project consisting of an analysis of a company's functional management areas and identifying potential improvements.

assessment_methods.method: Practical or project work (Group Project resolution)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 15% Group Project resolution + 25% Quizzes in the end of practical classes + 60% Closed book individual exam. The exam component requires a minimum classification of 7.5 out of 20. For eligibility to exams, students must attend 75% of classes where case studies and group projects are discussed. For special assessment cases (TE, DA), the grade is 60% closed book individual exam + 40% individual case study resolution, with the exam component also requiring a minimum of 7.5. Classification improvement is possible through an evaluation test for the Individual Exam component.
